- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion zones — if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast should be slightly below it.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out abrupt directional changes.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model tends to lag; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.5), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
